title: Phishing Email with Spoofed DocuSign Domain
id: 5a7d1a2e-3f9c-4b1a-8c2d-1e5f6a7b8c9d

arguments.summary: A critical Business Email Compromise (BEC) phishing attempt was reported by the CFO, involving display name spoofing of the CEO's identity to request an urgent wire transfer. The email contained no malicious links or attachments, representing a pure social engineering attack. The sender domain (corp-executive.com) and reply-to address (ProtonMail) are external and unaffiliated with the organization. Initial investigation revealed prior scanning activity from the same external IP (185.70.41.35), suggesting reconnaissance. No compromise was detected on the CFO's workstation. The incident was contained without escalation due to user vigilance and timely reporting.

timeline.description: External IP 185.70.41.35 conducted an Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged as low-severity event.
CFO receives spoofed email from 'ceo.name@corp-executive.com' with reply-to 'ceo.name@protonmail.com', requesting urgent wire transfer.
CFO reports suspicious email to SOC via user reporting channel.
SOC initiates investigation: IOC lookup confirms external origin of sender domain and IP. No malware detected in sandbox analysis of email artifacts.
EDR query on CFO's workstation (WS-EXEC-CFO) shows no suspicious processes or connections. User session appears normal.
SIEM search reveals 23 related events in past 7 days, including prior scan from same IP. No other phishing emails detected.
Containment actions attempted: firewall block and EPP quarantine denied due to policy restrictions. IAM action failed due to invalid parameters.
Incident classified as attempted BEC. No data breach or system compromise. User advised on social engineering risks.

The LNK, which attempted to execute a PowerShell command, was blocked by EDR on the endpoint. The source IP 91.234.99.41 has prior history of port scanning activity. timeline.description: Source IP 91.234.99.41 conducted a SYN scan against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected and logged by IDS.

Initial triage completed. IOC lookup on source IP and file hash performed. No prior malicious file reputation found. Process and file event data from endpoint collected.

SIEM search revealed 23 related events, primarily the earlier port scan from the same IP. Sandbox analysis returned a 'clean' verdict with a low risk score, indicating evasion techniques may have been used.
Admin phase initiated. Attempts to block the IP at the firewall, quarantine the endpoint, and reset user credentials were denied due to lack of approval and invalid parameters.

arguments.summary: An HTML smuggling phishing attack was detected and blocked. The email, spoofing a supplier invoice, delivered an HTML attachment that executed JavaScript to assemble and drop a malicious ISO file containing a LNK payload. The LNK attempted to execute a PowerShell command to download and run a script. EDR successfully prevented execution on the endpoint. Investigation revealed the source IP (91.234.99.41) had previously conducted an Nmap scan against an internal IT host. No other systems were found to have opened the attachment or executed the payload.

Malicious LNK file within ISO attempted to execute 'cmd.exe /c powershell -ep bypass -f extract.ps1'. EDR blocked the process creation.
Incident response initiated. EDR and SIEM investigations commenced.
Source IP linked to prior scanning activity. No other email recipients or payload executions identified.

arguments.summary: High-severity lateral movement attempt detected originating from Engineering workstation WS-ENG-022 (10.0.12.22) belonging to user d.chen. The host attempted SMB authentication to 15 hosts in the Finance VLAN within 3 minutes, with 3 successful logins. The activity is anomalous given the host's departmental location and lack of authorized access to Finance resources. Previous low-severity network scanning activity was observed from the same IP the prior day. UEBA scores remained low, indicating behavior within expected patterns, but the volume and target of SMB attempts represent a significant deviation. Immediate containment actions were denied during the Admin phase.

EDR query confirms no suspicious processes or network connections on WS-ENG-022 at time of alert.
SIEM search reveals 23 authentication events from 10.0.12.22 in past 24h; majority to non-Finance systems. 3 successful SMB logins to Finance hosts confirmed.
UEBA assessment: User d.chen has low anomaly score (0.35), but access to Finance VLAN is unauthorized and out of scope.
Containment actions (firewall block, account disable) requested but denied due to policy constraints.

The traffic pattern and signature 'chisel_client_v1.8' indicate use of the Chisel tunneling tool, suggesting an attempt to bypass network segmentation controls. The user involved was k.nakamura. Initial investigations found no malware in sandboxed samples, and prior activity on the host showed low risk. However, SIEM logs confirm repeated connections on the tunneling port. Mitigation actions were denied during the Admin phase due to lack of consensus.

timeline.description: Initial network scan detected from external source to IP 10.0.2.15 (later identified as misattribution due to CMDB mismatch).
Normal authentication event recorded for helpdesk user on WS-IT-101 (unrelated but logged on same IP due to CMDB error).
Anomalous RDP-over-SSH tunneling detected from WS-ENG-015 (10.0.12.15) to DMZ via tunnel on 10.0.200.10:8443. Chisel client signature identified.
SIEM correlation confirms 23 connection events matching tunneling pattern in past 24 hours.
EDR and UEBA checks show no malicious process trees or high-risk user behavior for k.nakamura; anomaly score 0.35 (low).
Sandbox analysis of related file hash returns clean verdict with risk score 0.8 (benign behavior).
Attempted firewall block and EPP quarantine actions denied due to lack of policy-based consensus.

The beacon established C2 communication and performed lateral movement via SMB to SRV-FILE-01. The user s.patel on WS-HR-001 was not the initial victim but was used as a pivot point, indicating credential compromise or pass-the-hash attack.

Command & Control: Beacon establishes HTTPS C2 communication with 198.51.100.23.
Discovery: Attacker enumerates network shares and identifies \\SRV-FILE-01\Finance\Q1-Reports.
Collection: Files copied and compressed into encrypted 7z archive.
Exfiltration: 2.3 GB archive uploaded to j.martinez.personal@gmail.com via dropbox.com.
Detection: DLP system triggers alert on large-scale upload of PCI/PII data.

arguments.summary: A critical data exfiltration attempt was detected and blocked on SRV-SQL-PROD-01. The attack began with a phishing compromise of user jsmith on WS-FIN-042, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon deployment. The attacker performed lateral movement, escalated privileges, and used stolen credentials of the svc-sql-prod service account to initiate a full dump of the customer_records database (4.2M rows). The 1.8GB dump was staged in /tmp and an SCP exfiltration attempt to 203.0.113.88 was blocked by the firewall. No data was exfiltrated. Root cause: phishing leading to credential compromise and lateral movement.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious mysqldump by Service Account
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: auditd
  category: process_creation
  definition: 'Process creation events from auditd'
detection:
  selection:
    - process_name: 'mysqldump'
      user_name: 'svc-*'
    - command_line|contains: 'mysqldump'
      user_name: 'svc-*'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/
description: Detects mysqldump execution by service accounts, which should not perform database exports.
author: SOC Team

    condition:
        all of them
}
